blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: The traveling thief problem (TTP) asks a thief to choose a tour and a packing together, and the benchmark of 9,720 instances of Polyakovskiy et al. (2014) is the standard test set for comparing TTP heuristics. We show that four of these instances are not TTP instances at all. Their files give a renting rate of 0.00, so the tour has no effect on the objective and each instance reduces to a 0-1 knapsack problem. One of them belongs to the 60 categorized instances on which new methods are usually compared, and on it five of nine published methods report exactly the same value. The cause is the format of the files, which keep the renting rate with two decimals, while the rule of the generator gives a rate close to 0.003 on these instances. The same rounding may shift the rate of 949 other instances by more than 1%. Since the tour and the packing used by the generator were not published, the original rates cannot be recovered. We therefore define new rates with the same rule, applied to a fully specified reference solution that we publish, and we show with a published heuristic that the corrected instances behave as TTP instances again. We also give reference results on the corrected instances and recommendations for future studies. Finally, we present ttplib, a new open-source Python library that loads any of the 9,720 instances, including the corrected ones, without downloading the whole benchmark.

blocks.zh: 2.2 国家 三份研究的零租金

blocks.en: Three studies published in the Journal of Heuristics show how the problem appears in practice.
blocks.zh: 在"高血压学报"上发表的三项研究报告显示了这个问题在实践中的出现.

blocks.en:
Wagner et al. (2018) studied 21 algorithms on all 9,720 instances and used the results to build algorithm
portfolios, which choose the best algorithm for an instance from features of the instance. They describe the case R = 0 R=0 in theory and note that the best solution is then the best solution of the knapsack part, but they do not point
out that four instances of the benchmark are in this case. These four instances were therefore treated as TTP
instances, both to compare the 21 algorithms and to train the portfolios, although the tour plays no role in them. The
rent itself is one of the instance features. In their analysis of feature importance, it is the second most important
feature for choosing an algorithm, after the capacity of the knapsack. Yet this feature is zero for the four instances,
and for 217 others it has a single significant digit (Section 2.4 ). The feature that the portfolios
rely on most after the capacity is thus missing for four instances and imprecise for many more.

blocks.en:
Namazi et al. (2023) proposed the CoCo variants, whose main idea is to coordinate the changes of the tour and of
the packing, and compared them with other methods on the categorized instances. On the instance of category A built on
dsj1000, this coordination cannot have any effect, since the tour does not change the value. Their Table 6 shows the
consequence. Over ten runs of each method, it gives a mean of 144,219 with a standard deviation of zero for
CS2SA ∗ , CoCoP and CoCoL, and a mean of 143,280 with a standard deviation of zero for MATLS. At its displayed
precision, the table thus reports no variation over ten runs for four methods, and three of them reach exactly the same
value. Their best value over all CoCo variants, 144,426 in their Table 5, is the optimal knapsack profit. For a fixed
packing, the value no longer depends on the tour, so a method that reaches the same packing in every run returns the
same value, whatever its tours. The zero rent does not force a method to find the same packing, but it removes the
effect of the tour, which is a main source of variation between runs. On this instance, the comparison therefore ranks
knapsack heuristics, not the coordination that the paper proposes. In our own experiments of
Section 3.3 with CoCoP, the ten runs on each corrected file gave ten different
values.

blocks.en: 3.1 Why the original values cannot be recovered

blocks.en:
A correction should ideally restore the value that the generator computed before rounding. This value cannot be
recovered from the files and code that Polyakovskiy et al. (2014a) published with the benchmark, for three
reasons. First, rule ( 3 ) depends on the tour, and the
authors of the benchmark distribute their tour only for the TSP instance a280. Their code does not contain the
generator, but it contains the call to linkern and the evaluation function, and we implemented the rule with
them, with the tour read from the output of linkern from the depot, the travel time computed as
in Eq. ( 2 ) and the knapsack solved exactly. With their tour, the recomputed rent of the 120 instances built on
a280 has a median ratio of 0.975 to the value in the file, and 90% of the ratios lie between 0.89 and 1.08. Rounded to
two decimals, it equals the value in the file on only one of the 120 instances, so the same implementation is close to
the files but does not reproduce them. Second, the rent changes with the tour, even among tours of almost the same
length. For each of the four instances, we ran linkern with ten seeds. The ten tours differ in length by less
than 1%, but with the same optimal packing the rent varies by up to 16% (Table 4 ), because the travel
time depends on where along the tour the heavy items are picked. Third, the rent changes with the optimal packing. A
knapsack can have several optimal packings with the same profit. On the bounded strongly correlated instance, two
optimal packings give rents that differ by 2.0% on the same tour, and the packing chosen by the original knapsack
solver ( Martello et al., 1999 ) is not known.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion and recommendations
blocks.zh: 5 结论和建议

blocks.en:
Four of the 9,720 instances of the standard TTP benchmark have a renting rate of 0.00 in their files. On these
instances, the tour has no effect on the objective, and the problem reduces to a 0-1 knapsack problem. One of them is
among the 60 categorized instances used in most comparisons of TTP heuristics, where it has measured the quality of
knapsack heuristics rather than the coordination of tour and packing. The zeros are consistent with the two decimals
with which the rents are stored, and the same format may remove much of the precision of the rent of many other
instances, mainly those built on TSP instances with long tours. The original rents cannot be recovered from the
files and code published with the benchmark, so we defined new rents for the four instances with the rule of the original generator, applied
to a fully specified reference solution that is published with them. With these rents, the four instances behave as
TTP instances again. The corrected instances, the reference solutions and the scripts are freely available, and the
library ttplib gives access to all 9,720 instances, including the corrected ones, without downloading the
whole benchmark.

blocks.en:
We make four recommendations for future work on this benchmark. 1. Studies that compare with published results should run the four instances with the original files ( R = 0.00 R=0.00 ),
since the published values were obtained on them, and say so. On the categorized instance, the optimal value
144,426 is then the best possible value. They should also run these instances with the corrected files and report
both results. The results on the corrected files will then build a base for comparisons on proper TTP instances in
future studies, starting from the reference results of Section 3.3 . 2. Studies that do not compare with published values should use the corrected files for these four instances, and
state the version used. 3. Results on instances with a small rent should be read with care, since the stored rent of these instances may
have lost much of its precision (Section 2.4 ). Among the categorized instances, this concerns four instances with a
relative rounding half-width above 5%. 4. Future generators of TTP instances should store the rent with enough significant digits to give back the computed
double-precision value, not with a fixed number of decimals. They should also publish the reference solution behind the
rent and a tolerance for checking it. A file can then be checked by evaluating this solution, whose objective must be
zero within the stated tolerance.
